title: incident-bot: fix oncall diagnostics priority weighting and fallback behavior
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes incorrect priority normalization that occasionally pushed high-urgency runbooks below low-relevance entries; improves fallback behavior when score components are missing.
description: Motivation: oncall diagnostics ranking was observed during a high-severity incident to deprioritize runbooks with high urgency when certain telemetry fields were missing. This caused slower mitigation for a subset of alerts. This PR normalizes priority weighting, makes score components robust to missing inputs, and introduces a deterministic fallback ordering to prefer SRE-verified runbooks.
changes_summary:
- Normalize weight vector on priority calculation so components sum to 1
- Treat missing telemetry fields as neutral (0.0) rather than zeroing weight contribution
- Add deterministic fallback: prefer runbooks tagged 'sre-verified' then 'official' then score
- Minor perf: cache computed weights per request window to avoid repeated allocations
- Add end-to-end integration tests and update runbook docs to surface new fallback behavior
commits: normalize: ensure priority weights are L1-normalized
fallback: deterministic ordering preferring sre-verified runbooks
robustness: treat missing score components as neutral (0.0)
perf: cache weights in request context
tests: add integration tests for missing telemetry fields and fallback ordering
docs: update diagnostics runbook behaviour notes
diff_snippets:
pkg/slo_toolkit/weights.go: -- if telemetry == nil { return 0 }
+ if telemetry == nil { component = 0.0 /* neutral */ }
cmd/incident-bot/main.go: add flag --prefer-sre-verified for rollout testing
review_comments: Lena Zhao (2024-10-21): Nice catch on the normalization bug — can you add a short benchmark to show the caching reduces allocations?
Asha Patel (2024-10-21): Added microbenchmark results to tests; caching reduces allocations ~3x under typical request window sizes.
Markus Reed (2024-10-22): Question: fallback ordering is a behavioral change. Are we confident this won't surface unexpected runbooks? Consider a config flag for customers.
Asha Patel (2024-10-22): Added --prefer-sre-verified flag and defaulted to true for now. Documented the flag in runbooks/diagnostics.md and added an entry to migration notes.
Lena Zhao (2024-10-23): CI green after rebase, LGTM. Approving.
Markus Reed (2024-10-23): Approved after small nits addressed.
testing: Added integration tests that simulate missing telemetry fields and verify fallback ordering. Microbenchmarks added under tests/benchmarks showing allocation reduction with caching. Manual QA: exercised on staging with live-ish SLOs and confirmed runbook ordering changes for affected alerts.
rollout_plan: Feature gated by flag --prefer-sre-verified (default true). Rollout: canary (5% traffic) for 24h, monitor oncall_ranking_latency and runbook_click_rate, then 50% for 48h before full.
known_issues: Edge case: customers with custom runbook tags other than 'sre-verified' may not immediately see expected ordering; will follow up with docs and migration guidance.
merge_details: Merged by squash (squash and merge) after approvals. No post-merge hotfix needed.
notes_for_release: Patch release: incident-bot v1.14.3. Addresses runbook ranking and robustness to missing telemetry fields. Recommended for SREs using runbook prioritization; incremental rollout recommended.
